#### Clase `WrappedSocket` (Línea 325)
- **Docstring:** _API-compatibility wrapper for Python's OpenSSL wrapped socket object.

Note: _makefile_refs, _drop(), and _reuse() are needed for the garbage
collector of PyPy._
- **Métodos:**
  - `def __init__(self, socket)` (Línea 333): Sin docstring.
  - `def _raise_on_error(self)` (Línea 352): A context manager that can be used to wrap calls that do I/O from
SecureTransport. If any of the I/O callbacks hit an exception, this
context manager will correctly propagate the exception after the fact.
This avoids silently swallowing those exceptions.

It also correctly forces the socket closed.
  - `def _set_ciphers(self)` (Línea 372): Sets up the allowed ciphers. By default this matches the set in
util.ssl_.DEFAULT_CIPHERS, at least as supported by macOS. This is done
custom and doesn't allow changing at this time, mostly because parsing
OpenSSL cipher strings is going to be a freaking nightmare.
  - `def _set_alpn_protocols(self, protocols)` (Línea 385): Sets up the ALPN protocols on the context.
  - `def _custom_validate(self, verify, trust_bundle)` (Línea 398): Called when we have set custom validation. We do this in two cases:
first, when cert validation is entirely disabled; and second, when
using a custom trust DB.
Raises an SSLError if the connection is not trusted.

wrapped socket, and shouldn't be needed in user code.
